D.t: Hannah Pingree leads by 12.7 in the forecast and wins 98% of simulations. The cushion is about 94,307 votes; a one point swing is about 3,704 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +5.1 and D +20.1. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +10.3. Your best recent poll is Maine People's Resource Center (D) at D +14.3; your worst is Marist College at R +2.0. 11 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Cumberland, a projected net 77,668 votes; York, a projected net 21,471 votes; Knox, a projected net 6,197 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Penobscot, R +7.3, 10.4% of the vote; Kennebec, D +1.6, 8.9% of the vote; Androscoggin, R +1.8, 7.1% of the vote; Oxford, R +7.3, 4.1% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Hannah Pingree runs furthest behind in Aroostook, Piscataquis, Somerset. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 95% of voters, 51 to 40, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.75 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 76% of voters, 53 to 39, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.83 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 65% of voters, 54 to 37, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.23 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Hannah Pingree: Immigration voters 19 to 72, Voters who can afford daily costs 46 to 45, Midsize counties 47 to 45. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$1.2M cash against $395K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
Registered Democrats cast 49% of the 207,285 ballots in Maine so far, against 21% for the other party. That is 0.7 points better for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.
Money: Raised $509K against $1.2M for Hannah Pingree.

R.t: Bobby Charles trails by 12.7 and wins 2% of simulations. Closing it takes about 47,153 voters switching sides, or 94,307 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +20.1 and D +5.1. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +10.3. Your best recent poll is Marist College at R +2.0; your worst is Maine People's Resource Center (D) at D +14.3. 11 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: Aroostook, a projected net 7,744 votes; Somerset, a projected net 5,952 votes; Penobscot, a projected net 5,604 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Penobscot, R +7.3, 10.4% of the vote; Kennebec, D +1.6, 8.9% of the vote; Androscoggin, R +1.8, 7.1% of the vote; Oxford, R +7.3, 4.1% of the vote.

R.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Bobby Charles runs furthest behind in York, Knox, Cumberland. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 95% of voters, 40 to 51, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.75 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 76% of voters, 39 to 53, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.83 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 65% of voters, 37 to 54, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.23 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Bobby Charles: Health care and Social Security voters 20 to 71, Large counties 24 to 68, Corruption voters 27 to 65. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$395K cash against $1.2M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.
